title: Binary and Docker Smoke Testing via selftest.py Addon
answers: How are mitmproxy standalone binaries tested after being built?
How is the Docker image validated during CI?
What does release/selftest.py do and how do you run it?
body:
The `release/` subsystem has no unit tests in `test/`. Smoke verification is performed via `release/selftest.py`, an in-process mitmproxy addon.
When `release/build.py:standalone_binaries` or `release/build.py:installbuilder_installer` builds an executable, it runs `release/build.py:_test_binaries`, which executes `{tool} -s release/selftest.py -p 0`.
In `release/selftest.py:load`, the server is configured to bind a random port (`listen_port = 0`). In `selftest.py:running`, an asyncio task sends an HTTPS request through the running proxy instance, validates the handshake and response, and triggers `ctx.master.shutdown()`.
Docker images run the same test in `.github/workflows/main.yml`: `docker run --rm -v $PWD/release:/release localtesting mitmdump -s /release/selftest.py`.
applies: Applies when verifying standalone binaries, installers, or Docker images produced by the release subsystem.
says: Standalone installer and container images should automatically verify they launch and handle traffic.
Docker container build published to registry fails basic proxy self test on startup.
